title: Amazon is taking its biggest shot at Nvidia yet with new TorchNeuron dev tool
summary: Amazon wants to break Nvidia’s hold on PyTorch, the free toolkit used to build most AI apps, so that more developers run their apps on alternative chips like its own.
author: Julie Bort

title: Hackers hit AI coding tool OpenCode, running up charges on users’ AI accounts
summary: OpenCode is an open-source AI coding agent that's become a popular alternative to Claude Code and Cursor. But hackers got into part of its online platform and stole some users’ API keys, and the AI tools it turned to for help kept refusing to look at the malicious code.
author: Aditya Mehta

title: Tolan snags $30M for its AI companion that helps users navigate life
summary: AI companion app Tolan has raised another $30 million after attracting more than 250,000 active users.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Replika’s founder built the AI assistant she pitched at Disrupt 12 years ago
summary: Eugenia Kuyda's newest startup Wabi is positioned to take advantage of an idea she had more than a decade ago. Wabi offers a personal AI assistant with a twist, free and downloadable to anyone today.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Tenstorrent hits $6.2B valuation to scale open-weight AI chips
summary: After drawing acquisition interest earlier this year, the Nvidia challenger raised $1.5 billion to remain independent.
author: Marina Temkin

title: People are using AI to make their smart TVs dumb again
summary: Fed up with ads, tracking, and sluggish interfaces, some smart TV owners are turning to AI agents to strip away bloatware and take back control of their TVs.
author: Sarah Perez

title: Nvidia launches new open models to run agents in the enterprise and on PCs
summary: Nvidia is leaning hard into the trend of enterprise companies wanting to run their own open models in their own data centers and also trying to make on-device, private AI agents a thing.
author: Julie Bort

title: Laplace Intelligence red-teams robots and self-driving cars before they hit the real world
summary: University of Michigan spinout Laplace Intelligence uses AI agents and interactive simulation to stress-test robots and self-driving vehicles before deployment. The profitable startup is competing in Startup Battlefield at TechCrunch Disrupt, October 13-15 in San Francisco.
author: Rebecca Bellan

title: Anthropic says it’s committing 5% of its shares to a ‘public benefit fund’
summary: The company offered some broad-strokes ideas for how this money might actually be used, such as “large donations to traditional nonprofits or direct distributions to specific populations.”
author: Anthony Ha

title: Disney agrees to hire the majority of Character AI’s workforce
summary: The filing also says that the “vast majority” of Character.AI employees who were offered jobs at Disney accepted them. However, this is a stalking horse bid, so another company could come forward with a higher offer.
author: Anthony Ha

title: Meta removes language that raised scraping and AI training concerns
summary: A Meta spokesperson insisted that the updated terms did not reflect a change in the way Meta crawls the web.
author: Anthony Ha

title: Anthropic says its workforce has become less junior and is spending more time in meetings
summary: The composition of Anthropic’s workforce and the type of work getting done have changed significantly in the past year.
author: Anthony Ha

title: Replit makes OpenAI its default over Anthropic, CEO says
summary: Masad said the decision was made for a number of different reasons, including cost. Replit announced a partnership with OpenAI in August, but there was never any indication that it was no longer partnering with Anthropic.
author: Kirsten Korosec, Lucas Ropek, Rebecca Bellan

title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
summary: The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.
author: Aditya Mehta

author: Theresa Loconsolo

summary: Amulya Vishwanath, who spent seven years leading product marketing for NVIDIA’s robotics platforms, says robotics is currently in its “Lego era,” with the basic building blocks like actuators, robotic hands, software, and safety standards still being rebuilt.  This view runs counter to tho
author: Theresa Loconsolo, Dominic-Madori Davis

title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
summary: According to Elorian's evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.
author: Aditya Mehta

title: Jev is Vercel’s fastest-adopted AI model ever
summary: The data comes from Vercel's AI gateway, a unified API service similar to OpenRouter.
author: Russell Brandom

title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
summary: Actor and angel investor Mark Wahlberg says he's OK with using AI in filmmaking, provided it's used "to enhance what you're doing."
author: Aisha Malik

title: Veritas expands its anti-counterfeit chip to jewelry, trophies, and fragrance bottles
summary: Counterfeiters are getting better at replicating brands' marks and passing off dupes, known as "superfakes," as genuine items. A startup called Veritas wants to tackle the problem with its own chip that verifies goods.
author: Ivan Mehta
